runs.scope: Two real TH09 rollback worlds and exact third-world input/hash/audit/framebuffer/Replay oracle; native ABI gestures; declared frontier transport delay; all worlds in one CPU-throttled renderer; not RTC, wall-clock input response, Launcher bridge or phone evidence

parameters.inputClock: Scheduled milliseconds converted from monotonic local capture slot / 60. This is a deterministic oracle stimulus, not independent wall-clock input.
parameters.transportClock: Receiving peer monotonic simulated frontier; bounded delivery-only tail after DEV frame limit

cpuThrottle.scope: All three same-origin worlds share this throttled renderer and execute sequentially. No per-peer CPU isolation or gameplay Hz claim.

runs.renderer: ANGLE (Intel, Intel(R) UHD Graphics (0x0000A78B) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)

oracle.wireVerification: Local retransmissions compare every byte of FrameInput, including touchUsed/unlimited/touchBomb flags and float bits. Confirmed spectator tuples independently compare buttons, motion kind including unlimited, x/y; spectator ABI has no separate touchUsed/touchBomb flags.
oracle.evidenceBoundary: Equality of the retained final hashes/audits and confirmed prefixes is rechecked; tape and retained Replay SHA values are recomputed from saved bytes. Framebuffer bytes and the other two Replay copies are absent, so their three-world equality remains a harness-reported assertion. Spectator tuples expose buttons/motion/x/y, not all wire flags.

recordedMeasured.method: Sequential explicit game_tick call work including all waits/recovery; not rAF or gameplay Hz. Legacy frame filters retained only for legacy profile.

capturePhases.method: Submitted phase mapped through actual wire frame minus input delay. Overall changes include phase entry; withinSegment excludes entry and requires same epoch. Numeric comparisons use exact JS !==, so +0/-0 are equal; bit changes remain separate. Control/game-state/float causality is not inferred.

recordedMeasured.method: Sequential explicit game_tick call work including all waits/recovery; not rAF or gameplay Hz. Legacy frame filters retained only for legacy profile.

capturePhases.method: Submitted phase mapped through actual wire frame minus input delay. Overall changes include phase entry; withinSegment excludes entry and requires same epoch. Numeric comparisons use exact JS !==, so +0/-0 are equal; bit changes remain separate. Control/game-state/float causality is not inferred.

observationClock.scope: Includes setup, all three worlds and oracle; not gameplay throughput.

limitations: Aggregate CPU occupancy does not establish single-core availability, CPU frequency, thermal state, GPU load, or a stable benchmark environment.
Process names are candidates for contention, not proof that a process is compiling. Known harness/relay/helper PIDs are labeled separately; other node processes remain unlabeled candidates.
Process CPU is cumulative lifetime CPU seconds. A first sighting is not CPU consumed during this run; PID reuse or counter reset can break a delta.
The 5 s process snapshots miss short tasks that start and exit between snapshots. Timer delays and source/receive times are retained.
This observer has overhead. Its own PowerShell helper is intentionally not a candidate process, but its work is included in aggregate CPU counters.
Overflow and sampling failures make this evidence incomplete; they are never a reason to silently remove a game result.
host.method: CPU occupancy uses legal counter-delta weights; no game sample is removed. Process CPU is lifetime seconds: only same pid/name in adjacent nonfailed snapshots contributes nonnegative deltas and paired source-clock intervals. Absence is not proven exit; truncation/failed snapshots and possible PID reuse remain visible. No wall-minus-CPU, compilation attribution, or per-call contention claim.

methods.allCalls: Every sampled game_tick(1) call in each rollback world is retained, including startup, waits and recovery; elapsed includes synchronous JS transport/tape hooks. Third-world oracle tick costs are not sampled here. No rewind-cursor filtering and no FPS computed from three-world setup/oracle wall time.
methods.recovery: For recovery rows: end = afterNext - (returnCode===1 ? 1 : 0); start = end - resimulatedDelta. Frame visits [start,end) join opponent 1-side actual captured wire to submitted capture-slot phase. Repeated visits count work; they do not prove which input caused correction. Whole call cost is only in exclusive restore-start buckets, never copied into every visited phase.
methods.reconstruction: Source-derived single game_tick formula, not an independently observed restore point. For correction rows, the harness stored depth from the same formula, so the reverse check is algebraically self-consistent. Cursor restore distance is beforeNext minus restoreStart, not necessarily predictionFrontier minus restoreStart during partial recovery. Continued-recovery rows and bounds remain checked.
methods.counters: stats[5] is SessionChannel RepairsSent: only SendRepairTo returning true increments it. Browser RTC success means send API accepted, not receipt or repair completion; browser relay returns false. This manual harness supplies a simulated transport. Return code 2 also covers not-ready, Prepare blockage, resource exit barriers and partial recovery, not solely missing network information.
methods.retainedLabels: recordedActivity.partialRecoveryCalls counts afterNext below beforeNext, not every unfinished recovery call. recordedMeasured and recordedActivity are preserved harness metadata. one-fresh still includes synchronous bridges/draw/audio; an exit prefix anchor may not have been simulated in that call. full12BFieldsValid checks wire/decoded-field consistency, not an independent complete ValidInput implementation.
methods.context: Top calls contain the original seven fields and both sides at logical frame anchors. These are input-frame context, not proof a fresh capture occurred in that call or wall-clock gesture/latency evidence. Source control context and numeric/bit changes are retained without assigning cause.
methods.scope: Deterministic native ABI, synthetic frame-delayed transport, three worlds in the same CPU-throttled renderer. Not real relay/direct networking, real phone, hosted touch bridge, input-to-visible latency or gameplay Hz. Unknown/failed runs remain; cross-run tape inequality is reported, not discarded.
